guard: The pure fragment is JavaScript: compound assignment applies its operator, update expressions return the right value, `for (let ...)` gives each iteration its own binding. (This suite is FAIL-FAST: `ok()` throws, so each mutation names the marker printed just UPSTREAM of the cell it breaks; the control cell is first and prints on every run.)
why: The defect that motivated this suite shipped SILENTLY in both halves: the validator never read
`node.operator` on an AssignmentExpression and the interpreter evaluated the right-hand side and
assigned it, so `x += 1` was admitted and executed as `x = 1` with no error anywhere. The only
loop in the old suite was written `attempt = attempt + 1`, so nothing pinned it. Each mutation
below reinstates one such drift and requires the differential cell that compares against node
to notice; a differential cell that stays green under a semantic mutation is measuring nothing.

mutations.name: compound assignment is plain assignment again
mutations.completionMarker: ok a program that logs a literal
mutations.note: The shipped defect, exactly. `let n = 10; n += 5` logged 5.

mutations.name: exponent evaluates as multiplication
mutations.completionMarker: ok a program that logs a literal
mutations.note: One operator wrong out of eighteen. The compound cell exponentiates (`n **= 3`), so it is the first to see it; the arithmetic cell would too.

mutations.name: postfix update returns the new value
mutations.find:
env.set(name, next, frame.depth);
          return prefix ? next : old;
mutations.expectRed: update expressions, prefix and postfix, on bindings and members
mutations.cell: update expressions, prefix and postfix, on bindings and members

mutations.name: a for loop shares one binding across iterations
mutations.completionMarker: ok if / else if / else, while, for, for-of, break, continue
mutations.note: The pre-existing behaviour: closures made in a `for (let ...)` body all watched the counter move. Nothing pinned it before, and no orchestration program is likely to hit it, but the claim under test is 'the pure fragment is JavaScript', not 'the likely part of it is'.

mutations.name: a thrown primitive is wrapped into a record on the way to catch
mutations.find:
if (e instanceof Error) return deepFreeze({ code: "L4000", kind: "host", message: e.message });
  return e;
mutations.expectRed: try / catch / finally with thrown records and rethrow
mutations.completionMarker: ok switch with braced and unbraced cases, default, fallthrough-free
mutations.cell: try / catch / finally with thrown records and rethrow
mutations.note: The pre-existing behaviour, found by this suite: `throw "inner"` reached `catch (e)` as `{ code: "L4000", kind: "thrown", message: "inner" }`.
